title: THE_DECISION_ENGINES
description: The open-source ecosystem is exploding with System 1 AI tools built around Jev. Fast, deterministic semantic logic.
content: 🗞️ issue 006: the decision engines (system one ai) everyone is obsessed with chatbots that can write a shakespearean sonnet, but real production software doesn't need poetry. it needs reliable, lightning-fast decisions. with the launch of typesafe ai's jev model, the industry is officially shifting toward "system one" ai: models designed to take unstructured data and output typed, probabilistic decisions instead of conversational strings. because jev is proprietary, an absolutely massive open-source ecosystem has exploded around it over the last week. developers are building autonomous web agents, trading bots, and developer tools that leverage this instant decision-making capability. jev is fast 20-200x faster, 40-400x cheaper (with output tokens free) and is optimized for decisions. a perfect development tool. here is how the open-source community is reacting to the system one movement. 🔬 the sandbox: 4 projects i tested this week 1. jev-ultrafast 🌐 (browser automation) what is it? the fastest open-source web agent ever built. by swapping out slow generative llms for jev's instant decision engine, it completely automates browser tasks (like filling forms or navigating uis) with near-zero latency. why you should care: if you've tried building autonomous browser agents before, you know they are painfully slow because they wait for llms to stream text. this framework makes agentic web scraping and testing instantaneous. my rating: absolute game changer 5/5 ⭐ website: github.com/browser-use/jev-ultrafast 💻 get started: bash git clone https://github.com/browser-use/jev-ultrafast.git 2. fast-jev-compaction ⚡ (developer tooling) what is it? a brutal, high-speed plugin for claude code. instead of having claude waste expensive tokens trying to "summarize" your long terminal history, it uses jev to instantly score every single tool call and automatically drops the useless ones while keeping the critical logs verbatim. why you should care: it completely stops your ai coding assistants from losing context in massive codebases and drastically cuts down your anthropic api bills. my rating: essential infrastructure 5/5 ⭐ website: github.com/tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction 💻 get started: bash npm install -g fast-jev-compaction 3. jev-trader 📉 (high-frequency trading) what is it? a hardcore, open-source trading bot that makes exactly one ai trade decision every single monad block using jev on kuru mon-usdc. why you should care: crypto trading on monad requires insane speed. you physically cannot do this with openai or anthropic due to their generation latency, making this the ultimate flex for jev’s sub-15ms response times. my rating: strong 4/5 ⭐ website: github.com/jarrodwatts/jev-trader 💻 get started: bash git clone https://github.com/jarrodwatts/jev-trader.git 4. shapeshift 🪄 (dynamic ui) what is it? an input field that becomes exactly what you mean. it provides a single text box that instantly morphs into the correct ui component as you type. it is powered by typesafe jev and incredibly, works entirely offline. why you should care: this is a glimpse into the future of user interfaces. instead of building massive, complicated forms, you give the user one input box and let the decision model instantly route and render the exact components they actually need. my rating: pure magic 5/5 ⭐ website: github.com/anishfn/shapeshift 💻 get started: bash npm install shapeshift-ui ☕ the curious non-dev: no code required what exactly is "system 1 vs system 2" ai? if you are confused by all this jargon, think of daniel kahneman’s famous psychology book, thinking, fast and slow. system 2 is your slow, methodical brain. if someone asks you to solve 17 x 24, you have to stop and work it out. this is exactly what chatgpt and claude are doing—slowly generating reasoning, one word at a time. system 1 is your fast, instinctive brain. if someone throws a baseball at your head, you don't calculate the wind resistance; you just duck. jev is a "system 1" ai. it doesn't write essays; it just looks at data and instantly makes a hard decision. and for most software, that is infinitely more useful. 📡 the radar: 12 more projects to spin up this weekend 🧠 the clones (system one alternatives) laya - a massive, non-autoregressive open-weights system 1 decision engine supporting 100+ languages. semif-openjev - semantic "if statements" built from open models that you can run completely locally on a 3090 gpu at home. nanojev - a nano replica of jev featuring parallel decisions, dynamic candidates, and an open end-to-end training pipeline. kev - a family of tiny, lightning-fast decision models that clone jev's architecture but can run 100% locally on your own mac. 🤖 agentic workflows (the routers) quantdinger - an open-source ai trading os that heavily integrates jev for high-speed agent trading and backtesting across crypto and stocks. jev-router - a tool that uses jev to dynamically route your prompts to the cheapest/fastest llm model in claude code for any given task. hermes-jev-skills - jev-powered model routing, memory compaction, and skill selection for hermes, claude code, and codex agents. minecraft-agent - an astra planner and jev controller for minecraft that natively records and verifies run routes. 🧰 ecosystem & developer tools awesome-jev - the massive curated list of public projects, integrations, and discussions built on jev. hippo-memory - biologically-inspired memory for ai agents (with decay and consolidation) that uses a hosted jev endpoint as an ultra-fast reranker. jev-chat-jarvis - a wild non-invasive screen reader that uses jev to read your chat apps and suggest auto-replies without hooking into the app. jev-review - a staged code-review workflow and local dashboard built entirely around typesafe jev. 🏗️ closing thoughts we are witnessing a fundamental shift in how developers build with ai. we are finally moving past the era of begging a chatbot to return a properly formatted json object, and moving into the era of deterministic, lightning-fast semantic logic. the projects featured this week prove that when you remove the latency of text generation, you can automate almost anything. i'd love to hear what incredible open-source projects you are spinning up this weekend—reach out on x (twitter) or linkedin and let me know! until next thursday, keep your servers close and support your local maintainers.

title: THE_DATA_EXTRACTION_BLUEPRINT
description: Data is the new oil, but most of it is trapped in terrible formats. Learn how to extract, clean, and weaponize it.
content: 🗞️ issue 005: the data extraction blueprint data is the new oil, but right now, most of it is trapped in terrible formats, locked behind paywalls, or buried in unstructured pdfs. if you want to build anything meaningful in the age of ai, you need to know how to extract, clean, and weaponize data faster than anyone else. this week, we are opening the data extraction blueprint. we are covering 3 categories of data manipulation: the scraping arsenal, database oddities, and the data janitors. grab your coffee. open your terminal. let's start scraping. 🔬 the sandbox: 3 projects i tested this week 1. crawl4ai 🕷️ (the scraping arsenal) what is it? the ultimate open-source web crawler built specifically for large language models. it bypasses anti-bot protections, executes javascript, and strips out all the junk html to return clean, structured markdown ready for your ai agents. why you should care: instead of spending hours writing custom beautifulsoup scripts that break every time a website updates its css, this single tool turns any complex web page into pristine training data in seconds. my rating: absolute game changer 5/5 ⭐ website: github.com/unclecode/crawl4ai 💻 get started: bash pip install crawl4ai 2. sqlmap 🗺️ (database oddities) what is it? the undisputed, open-source king of automated sql injection and database takeover. it is an industrial-grade penetration testing tool that detects and exploits database vulnerabilities across every major sql engine on the planet. why you should care: before you deploy your next startup backend, point this at your own staging server. it will aggressively test your application's armor and immediately expose any endpoints where data can be easily stolen. my rating: frighteningly powerful 5/5 ⭐ website: github.com/sqlmapproject/sqlmap 💻 get started: bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/sqlmapproject/sqlmap.git sqlmap-dev 3. nougat 🍫 (the data janitors) what is it? an incredible machine learning model released by meta (facebook research) that visually understands academic pdfs and converts them perfectly into markdown, preserving complex latex math equations and data tables. why you should care: pdfs are where data goes to die. if you are building a rag application or a custom ai, nougat completely eliminates the nightmare of parsing scientific papers and tables into readable text. my rating: essential infrastructure 4.5/5 ⭐ website: github.com/facebookresearch/nougat 💻 get started: bash pip install nougat-ocr ☕ the curious non-dev: no code required scraping without writing a line of code: meet maxun. web scraping usually requires writing complex python scripts to navigate around pop-ups and logins. if you don't know how to code, this used to be a massive barrier. or maybe not if you're cozy with llms. enter maxun. it is an open-source, no-code web data extraction platform. you simply navigate a website in your browser, click on the text or images you want to extract, and it automatically builds a robot to scrape that data into a spreadsheet for you. it even handles pagination and scroll-loading automatically. 📡 the radar: 12 more projects to spin up this weekend 🕷️ the scraping arsenal linkedin_scraper - extracts detailed linkedin profiles, jobs, and company data for osint. google-maps-scraper - a stealthy scraper for extracting business emails and social profiles from maps. staffspy - a targeted corporate data scraper for aggregating employee information. gospider - a blazing fast web spider written in go that parses javascript urls and finds hidden subdomains. 🗺️ database oddities libsql - an open-source, highly scalable distributed fork of sqlite optimized for the edge. teleport - access your remote databases, kubernetes clusters, and ssh servers securely without needing a vpn. py-pglite - spins up an instant, real postgresql database directly inside python for blazing-fast testing. schemaspy - automatically generates gorgeous, interactive entity-relationship diagrams from your raw database schemas. 🍫 the data janitors unstract - an open-source platform that uses llms to structure data from completely unstructured documents. flow - a brilliant low-memory data pipeline framework for php developers handling massive datasets. lerobot-data-studio - a visual web gui for scrubbing, cleaning, and validating robotics training datasets. voice_datasets - a comprehensively curated repository of over 95 open-source voice datasets for training audio models. 🏗️ closing thoughts we are living in an era where the company with the cleanest dataset wins. you don't need a massive team to build an incredible product anymore—you just need to know how to scrape the right data, parse the terrible formats, and feed it into an open-source model. the tools are free; the only barrier is your willingness to build. i'd love to hear what your arsenal is when scraping—reach out on x (twitter) or my rating: flawless 5/5 ⭐ - website: github.com/debpalash/voicestudio - get started: bash git clone https://github.com/debpalash/voicestudio.git 2. facefusion 🎭 (the visual illusionists) what is it? the next-generation face swapper and enhancer. it completely automates the incredibly tedious process of mapping facial landmarks across moving video frames, allowing you to swap faces with near-perfect lighting and blending. - my rating: frighteningly good 4.5/5 ⭐ - website: github.com/facefusion/facefusion - get started: bash git clone https://github.com/facefusion/facefusion.git 3. deep-live-cam 🔴 (the visual illusionists) what is it? the viral titan of august 2026. this repo allows you to do real-time face swapping during a live webcam feed (like a zoom call or twitch stream) using only a single image of the target face. - my rating: absolute game changer 5/5 ⭐ - website: github.com/hacksider/deep-live-cam - get started: bash git clone https://github.com/hacksider/deep-live-cam.git --- ☕ the curious non-dev: no code required how to defend against voice cloning scams with tools like openvoice requiring just 3 seconds of audio to perfectly mimic a loved one, "grandparent scams" (where scammers call acting like a family member in distress) are skyrocketing. you don't need code to protect yourself, you need a protocol and a bit of scepticism. establish a "safe word" with your family. if someone calls from an unknown number, even if they sound exactly like your spouse, child, or parent—ask for the safe word. ai can clone a voice perfectly, but it cannot guess a pre-established offline secret. want to test for yourself? voicestudio can be downloaded here: voicestudio and you can support facefusion by buying windows or mac installers here: facefusion --- 📡 the radar: 12 more projects to spin up this weekend 🗣️ the voice cloners 1. bark (31,200+ stars) - a transformer-based text-to-audio model created by suno. it can generate highly realistic, multilingual speech as well as background noise, simple sound effects, and non-verbal communications like laughing and sighing. 2. rvc-webui - the wildly popular framework for real-time voice conversion. 3. cosyvoice - multi-lingual voice cloning built by alibaba's funaudiollm team. 4. tts - a massive, foundational deep learning toolkit for text-to-speech. 🎭 the visual illusionists 1. deepfacelab (45,100+ stars) - the absolute gold standard of deepfake creation. this is the heavy-duty software used by 95% of deepfake creators online. 2. roop (25,300+ stars) - one-click face replacement in video (the spiritual predecessor to facefusion). 3. sd-webui-reactor - the definitive fast and simple face swap extension for stable diffusion. 4. rope - a gui-focused deepfake app built on insightface that allows for multiple face swapping in a single video. 🧍 the digital avatars 1. sadtalker (10,500+ stars) - learning realistic 3d motion coefficients for stylized audio-driven single-image talking face generation. 2. emo - emote portrait alive: generating expressive portrait videos strictly from audio. 3. v-express - tencent's open-source framework for conditional dropout in audio-driven talking face generation. 4. musetalk - real-time, high-quality audio-driven lip-syncing for digital avatars. --- 🏗️ closing thoughts the pace at which open-source ai is democratizing these capabilities is breathtaking. while the ethical implications of this tech are profound and absolutely warrant caution, hiding from the technology won't stop it from advancing. as developers, the best way to understand the threat landscape of deepfakes and ai impersonation is to pull the repositories, run the models, and see the architecture with our own eyes. i'd love to hear what incredible open-source projects you are spinning up this weekend—reach out on x (twitter) or linkedin and let me know! until next thursday, find safe words with your loved ones and don't be fooled by the digital "you". and also support your local maintainers.

title: THE_SHADOW_ECOSYSTEM
description: A look into Local AI, Video Editing, and the breakout 'Hot Summer' Repos of August 2026.
content: 🗞️ issue 002: the shadow ecosystem if you are still paying monthly subscriptions for chatgpt or capcut, you need to see the open-source tools that just went viral this month. we have household-name cloud platforms that edit our videos, write our code, and manage our apis. but behind the massive marketing budgets of those tech giants, there is an entire shadow ecosystem of open-source projects bringing that exact same power to your local machine for free. based on your feedback from last week, we are mixing things up to bring you more diversity. today, we are deep-diving into 3 vastly different categories: local ai, video editing, and the "hot summer" repos (the absolute most-starred breakout projects of august 2026). we are showcasing just 3 incredible tools in the sandbox, followed by a section specifically for non-developers, and 12 extra projects for your weekend radar. grab your coffee. open your terminal. let's start testing. --- 🔬 the sandbox: 3 projects i tested this week 1. ollama ⚓ (local ai) what is it? the absolute easiest way to get up and running with large language models locally. it packages complex models and apis into a single, flawless developer experience so you can run ai completely offline. out of the box, it lets you pull and run powerhouse open-weight models like meta's llama 3, google's gemma, mistral, and microsoft's phi-3 with a single command. - my rating: perfect 5/5 ⭐ - website: ollama.com - get started: bash curl -fssl https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh 2. opencut 🎬 (video editing) what is it? a ridiculously powerful open-source video editor that is finally giving capcut a run for its money. it brings hardware-accelerated, professional non-linear editing to the masses without the monthly subscription. - my rating: loved it 4.5/5 ⭐ - website: github.com/opencut-app/opencut - get started: bash git clone https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut.git 3. deepseek harness 🔥 (the "hot summer" august 2026 breakout) what is it? the absolute undisputed king of github this august with over 196,000+ stars. deepseek harness operates on the philosophy that "everything is a plugin". it's a wildly extensible agent ecosystem that is taking the developer world by storm. - my rating: game changer 5/5 ⭐ - website: github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness - get started: bash git clone https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness.git --- ☕ the curious non-dev: no code required a section dedicated to our readers who love tech but don't want to stare at a command line. if reading about "local llms" and "gpu acceleration" sounds intimidating, i have great news: you do not need to be a programmer to run your own private ai. if you want the "chatgpt experience" completely offline and completely private, all you need to do is download a tool called lm studio. it’s completely free. you install it just like you would install any application on you computer. once you open it, you can browse and download hundreds of ai models with a single click. it gives you a beautiful, familiar chat interface where you can talk to the ai completely offline. no subscription fees, no internet connection required, and no tech giant reading your chat logs. be mindful that not all models will be supported on your device depending on hardware architecture, quality and pricing of your machine. --- 📡 the radar: 12 more projects to spin up this weekend looking for your next weekend project? here are 12 more incredible tools pushing the boundaries of what open-source can do. 🧠 local ai wranglers 1. openclaude-portable - run a full, completely offline ai coding agent directly from a usb flash drive. 2. mercury agent skills - a library that injects 131 specialized skills directly into your local ai agents. 3. droid-llm-hunter - combines static analysis with local llms to automatically hunt down vulnerabilities in android applications. 4. chatgarment - generates complete 3d garments and clothing assets purely from text prompts using local models. 🎬 open-source video & media 1. yt-dlp - the undisputed king of video downloading. a ridiculously powerful command-line tool that can pull high-res media from almost any site on the internet. 2. ffmpeg (63,600+ stars) - the absolute backbone of modern digital media. a massive, foundational suite of libraries and programs for handling video, audio, and multimedia streams. 3. remotion (57,300+ stars) - a massive framework that lets you build, render, and orchestrate videos programmatically using standard react and css. 4. losslesscut (43,200+ stars) - the ultimate swiss army knife of lossless video editing. snip, trim, and combine instantly without re-encoding. 🔥 august 2026 "hot summer" breakouts 1. grok-build (26,000+ stars) - spacexai's coding agent harness and tui. fullscreen, mouse interactive, and highly extensible. 2. anydoc (18,500+ stars) - built in rust, this tool seamlessly converts word, powerpoint, excel, and pdfs into clean markdown. 3. watermarks-remover (18,400+ stars) - strips multi-vendor ai provenance marks, c2pa metadata, and invisible watermarks from files. 4. openworker (15,900+ stars) - the brand new, highly anticipated open-source agent framework from andrew ng. --- 🏗️ closing thoughts: the value of the shadows my sandbox methodology is strict. every week, i spin up fresh environments and dive into these codebases looking for time-to-value, community spirit, and that magical "wait, this is free?" factor. we feature these projects not to tear down the cloud apis we rely on, but to lift up the unsung heroes building in the shadows. the open-source community is the bedrock of the next generation of the internet. every tool we covered today is a gift to everyone, built by people who simply wanted to solve a problem and share the solution. there are no sponsorships as this newsletter is a personal project closed to heart and i reserve the right to my own opinions and experiences when testing these projects. i'd love to hear what incredible open-source projects you are spinning up this weekend—reach out on x (twitter) or linkedin and let me know! until next thursday, don't forget to git push before going home and support your favorite maintainers.

title: TAKING_CONTROL_BACK
description: A deep dive into 8 tools that let you replace expensive SaaS subscriptions.
content: 🗞️ issue 001: taking control back welcome to issue 001 of the terminal thursday. this week, we're talking about taking control back. as developers, we are incredibly lucky to live in a golden age of saas. we have beautiful, household-name platforms that host our code, manage our notes, and secure our networks seamlessly. we've built careers and businesses on top of libraries, tools and code maintained by the silent heroes of open-source software. i love the saas ecosystem as it has pushed the entire industry forward. but what happens when you decide to bring it all back home? this week, we are exploring the tools that let you replace expensive saas subscriptions, cloud drives, and privacy-invading analytics platforms with your own infrastructure. we’re leading with three absolute titans of open-source independence that you likely already know (and should definitely be using), before diving into five brilliant, obscure hidden gems i dug up and tested this week. grab your coffee. open your terminal. let's take back control. 🔬 the sandbox: 8 projects i personally tested this week 1. supabase ⚓ (the open-source giants) supabase has firmly established itself as an absolute marvel of open-source engineering. i’ve deployed it on countless projects, but spinning it up locally via docker this week for a quick prototype reminded me exactly why i'm amazed with this team. they've packaged postgres, auth, instant apis, and edge functions into an open ecosystem with a developer experience that is simply flawless. it’s a masterclass in community-driven infrastructure. 🔗 check out supabase 2. home assistant ⚓ (homelab paradises) i spent my entire saturday migrating my remaining smart devices off their proprietary cloud bridges and into a local home assistant instance running on a dusty raspberry pi 2. the sheer dedication of the thousands of contributors who have built integrations for almost every device on the planet is staggering. home assistant is the gold standard for taking back control of your smart home, built entirely by a community that cares. 🔗 check out home assistant 3. pi-hole ⚓ (the privacy advocates) there is nothing quite as satisfying as firing up pi-hole and watching it silently protect your network from background tracking requests in real-time. the fact that a dedicated group of volunteers built and maintains a dns sinkhole that protects entire networks without requiring a single piece of client-side software is a testament to the open-source ethos. it's the ultimate network bodyguard, gifted to the world for free. and it runs smoothly on a pi zero w. 🔗 check out pi-hole 4. semantica 💎 (the open-source giants) this was the absolute standout of my week. semantica is an open-source data orchestration layer that feels like enterprise-grade intelligence software. i spun it up locally just to feed it some test data, and the context graphing is insanely powerful. seeing this level of data visualization and architecture built out in the open, accessible to anyone on their own machine, felt like pure magic. 🔗 check out semantica 5. localsend 💎 (the open-source giants) airdrop is brilliant, right until you need to send a file to an android phone or a windows pc. enter localsend. i installed it across my mac and an old android test device, and the cross-platform file sharing is seamless. it’s entirely local: no cloud, no internet connection required. the developers behind this saw a walled-garden problem and built a beautiful, universal bridge for everyone to use. 🔗 check out localsend 6. batear 💎 (the privacy advocates) i'm a sucker for hardware projects that push boundaries. batear is an ultra-low-cost acoustic drone detector that runs entirely on the edge via an esp32-s3 microcontroller. i flashed it onto a spare esp32 i had lying around. it operates with zero internet connection, relying strictly on acoustic signatures and sending alerts via encrypted lora. it's a brilliant, creative use of open hardware and software. 🔗 check out batear 7. vaultsync 💎 (homelab paradises) as an (relatively) new obsidian user, syncing my vault has been a puzzle i wanted to solve locally. vaultsync solves this elegantly by offering a self-hosted sync for iphone and ipad, routing peer-to-peer over syncthing. i kept my notes 100% local and they synced flawlessly. i am incredibly grateful to developers who build niche, privacy-focused tools like this purely to solve a community need. 🔗 check out vaultsync 8. operately 💎 (the open-source giants) if you love the polished ux of tools like notion or linear, operately brings that exact level of polish to an open-source company operating system. i deployed it on a small vps just to kick the tires, and the ui is shockingly good. it feels like a modern, opinionated startup os built by people who poured their heart and soul into the workflow experience. 🔗 check out operately --- 📡 the radar: more projects to spin up this weekend 🦣 the open-source giants posthog ⚓ - an incredibly powerful, community-driven product analytics platform. cal.com ⚓ - open-source scheduling that rivals the best premium tools on the market. 🏠 homelab paradises nextcloud ⚓ - the classic, all-in-one productivity suite built by thousands of contributors. jellyfin ⚓ - the completely free, open-source media server. 🕶️ the privacy advocates tailscale ⚓ - wireguard made wonderfully easy. bitwarden ⚓ - the industry-standard open-source password manager. --- 🌟 closing thoughts: the value of the shadows you might be wondering: how do i actually evaluate these tools before featuring them here? my sandbox methodology is strict, but it comes from a place of deep respect. every week, i spin up a fresh docker environment and dive into these codebases. i look for three things: 1. time-to-value: how quickly can i experience the "magic"? if i get a "hello world" in under 15 minutes, the dx is truly shining. 2. community spirit: does the project welcome you in? is the documentation written with care? 3. the "wait, this is free?" factor: when a solo developer ships a ui/ux so polished that it rivals a venture-backed startup, it deserves to be celebrated. we feature these projects not to tear down the saas providers we rely on, but to lift up the unsung heroes building in the shadows. i'd love to hear what incredible open-source projects you are spinning up this weekend—reach out on x (twitter) or linkedin and let me know! until next thursday, keep your servers close and support your local maintainers.
